title: Aseptic Preservation, Hurdle Technology, Hydrostatic Pressure Technology and Microwave Processing
shortDescription: Sterile fill, combining barriers, pressure-based processing and microwave heating.
genZNote: Sterilise the food and the pack separately, then marry them in a clean room. Hurdle tech is just 'many small barriers beat one big wall'.

sections.heading: Aseptic Preservation
bullets: Product is sterilised (UHT/HTST, ohmic), cooled and filled into pre-sterilised containers in a sterile environment, then hermetically sealed.
Packaging sterilised by hydrogen peroxide, steam or radiation; Tetra Pak and Elopak are widely used cartons; products: UHT milk, juices, soups, tofu, purees; shelf life months at ambient temperature.
Benefits: better colour/flavour than in-container sterilisation; critical control: sterile zone integrity, seal integrity and flow-through heat treatment validation.

sections.heading: Hurdle Technology
bullets: Concept by Leistner: combining several mild preservation factors (hurdles) — temperature, aw, pH, redox, preservatives, competitive flora, packaging — so microbes cannot overcome all of them (hurdle effect, metabolic exhaustion).
Examples: Indian pickles (salt, acid, oil), intermediate-moisture foods, minimally processed fruits (mild heat + acid + MAP + cold).
Advantage: retain nutrition and sensory quality; requires careful design and validation.

sections.heading: Hydrostatic Pressure Technology
sections.body: Hydrostatic (isostatic) high-pressure processing exposes packaged foods to ~300–600 MPa in a water-filled vessel; pressure transmits uniformly regardless of shape (Le Chatelier's principle) so there is no thermal gradient. It inactivates vegetative microbes and some enzymes; spores need pressure-assisted thermal sterilisation (PATS). Unit operation details are in the Non-Thermal lesson.

sections.heading: Microwave Processing
bullets: Frequencies: 2450 MHz (domestic) and 915 MHz (industrial); heating arises from dipolar rotation of water and ionic conduction.
Features: rapid volumetric heating, uneven heating (hot/cold spots), poor browning; uses: tempering, drying, pasteurisation/sterilisation of packaged foods, cooking.
Safety: use microwave-safe packaging; metals cause arcing; stir/stand time equalises temperature.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Aseptic processing, hurdle technology, hydrostatic pressure and microwave heating are advanced ways to preserve foods with improved quality retention.

highYieldFacts: Microwave heating is volumetric but non-uniform.
commonTraps: Do not say microwaves heat from outside only.
